sections.h2: Which Huntington office bills my property tax?
sections.html:
Two town offices split the job. The Assessor sets values on the 72,500-plus parcels in Huntington and its villages. The Receiver of Taxes prints the bills and collects payment. The Town Board appoints the Assessor, and voters elect the Receiver.

You will find the Receiver at Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street, Huntington, NY 11743, phone 631-351-3217. The same office handles money for the town, Suffolk County, the school districts and other special districts, and it also accepts Dix Hills Water District payments. Rates and assessments are not its call. It simply collects under the state Real Property Tax Law and the Suffolk County Tax Act.

Payment counters keep weekday hours of 9 am to 4 pm. For general questions the office stays open longer, from 8 am to 5:30 pm.

sections.h2: When Huntington property taxes are due
sections.html:
You get one bill, mailed in the second week of December. For 2026/27 the first half is due January 10, 2027, and the second half is due May 31, 2027. January 10, 2027 lands on a Sunday, and a weekend due date rolls to the next business day. Town Hall also posts extended payment hours until 7 pm on June 1, 2027.

Some owners get a few extra days on the second half. Basic STAR recipients have until June 4, 2027, and so do seniors on the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR. After June 1, those seniors can pay only by mail or at the counter.

Mail has become riskier. A federal postmark change effective December 24, 2025 means a letter dropped in a mailbox may carry a later date than the day you sent it. Only a hand-canceled stamp from a post office counter is a sure thing, and the tax office has no power to forgive a penalty on a payment that arrived late and carries no timely postmark. Better options are online payment (third-party fees apply), the payment line at (877) 690-3729 using jurisdiction code 2012 and your 8 digit bill number, the counter at Town Hall, or the locked black box there.

sections.h2: What a late first-half payment costs
sections.html:
Interest starts at 1% on January 11 and rises a point each month, topping out at 5% in the last three weeks of May.

Interest on a late first-half payment, 2026/27
Paid betweenInterest
December 1 to January 10None
January 11 to February 101%
February 11 to March 102%
March 11 to April 103%
April 11 to May 104%
May 11 to May 315%

Once May 31 passes, the town stops accepting the tax. You then pay the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, (631) 852-3000. The bill there carries a 5% penalty plus interest of 1% a month, counted from February 1. Because that interest keeps running, a house with an old balance gets more expensive to clear every month it sits.

sections.h2: How to file a Huntington assessment grievance
sections.html:
Your complaint goes to the Town Assessor's Office, Room 100 at Town Hall, phone (631) 351-3226, and it must be in by Grievance Day. That is the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027.

  • The taxable status date is March 1, and the house is valued as it stood that day.
  • The tentative roll is set and open for public viewing on May 1.
  • Forms and a fact sheet are available after April 1. Only an originally signed form is accepted, so a fax or an email will be rejected.
  • If the Board of Assessment Review turns you down, you can take the dispute to court. New York State lists a $30 fee for Small Claims Assessment Review, and the window is 30 days from the final roll.

Suffolk boards sit earlier than boards in most of the state, which use the fourth Tuesday. If you count on the later date, you will miss the Huntington deadline.

Every exemption runs through the Assessor's Office. File by March 1 and the savings show up on the December bill that follows. Programs include:

  • Senior Citizens Limited-Income, for owners aged 65 or older, with an income ceiling of $58,400 for both town and county and a deduction for documented medical costs.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income, filed by the same March 1 date.
  • Military service exemptions: Alternative, Cold War, Eligible Funds and Gold Star Parent.
  • Home Improvement, which phases in the added assessment from a renovation over nine years, up to 400 in assessment.

Basic and Enhanced STAR belong to the state, so questions about them go to the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance at 518-457-2036. An exemption stays with the person who earned it. A buyer who qualifies has to apply separately after closing, so mention that when you negotiate.

sections.h2: Selling a Huntington house when tax is owed
sections.html:
Tax stays with the parcel, so closing requires an up-to-date number. The Receiver's office keeps the tax rolls, ownership changes and a list of arrears. Before you sign a contract, ask which half of the current bill has been paid.

If the 2026/27 bill is still open when you list, two dates control your plan. Up to May 31, 2027 the Receiver takes payment. Past that date the tax, penalty and interest go to the county comptroller in Riverhead, and the total grows by 1% each month. Get the payoff in writing from whichever office holds the debt, and have it written onto the closing statement.

  1. Call 631-351-3217 and ask for the status of both halves.
  2. Ask whether a Dix Hills Water District balance sits next to the tax bill.
  3. If the debt has moved to the comptroller, request that office's figure through your expected closing date.
  4. Give both figures to your closing attorney.

A buyer paying cash can close quickly and clear the tax at the table. That suits owners in Huntington Station, Dix Hills or Greenlawn who have fallen behind and want the matter settled without waiting on a retail listing.

Huntington lies on the North Shore of Long Island, with Long Island Sound to its north and Nassau County to its west. Four villages sit inside the town: Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport. Hamlets include Dix Hills, Melville, Commack, Greenlawn and Huntington Station.

The town counts 205,891 residents as of July 2025, in 71,542 households. About 88.7% of homes are owner-occupied, with a median value of $715,600. Median household income is $168,029 and median rent is $2,358. Homes carry high values, which makes each month of 1% interest cost real money.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Huntington property tax due in 2027?
faqs.a: May 31, 2027, with extended hours on June 1, 2027. Owners on Basic STAR, the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR have until June 4, 2027.

faqs.q: Where do I pay late Huntington property tax after May 31?
faqs.a: Send it to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. Their number is (631) 852-3000, and the bill adds a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: What is Grievance Day in Huntington?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday of May, which is May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office needs your originally signed complaint on or before that day. Faxed and emailed copies are rejected.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a senior exemption in Huntington?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at (631) 351-3226 to join the mailing list, then file with proof of income by March 1. The income limit is $58,400.

faqs.q: Does the Huntington Receiver of Taxes set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver only collects and distributes the money. Rates and assessments are set elsewhere.
